To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

dehydration causes a rapid, transient rise in renal ornithine-decarboxylase (renal-ODC) activity, that adrenalectomy and propylthiuracil (PTU) treatment have no effect on renal-ODC activity, that AVP injection causes a rapid, short-lived rise in renal-ODC, and that gonadectomy (acutely) reduces renal-ODC and blunts the renal-ODC response to AVP.
the kidney ornithine decaboxylase (ODA) response to dehydration is mediated by mechanisms other than those involved in the regulation of arginine vasopressine (AVP) secretion.

1) dehydration causes a marked increase in kidney ornithine decaboxylase activity in the mouse, and that this effect is not due to AVP; 2) AVP injection causes a rapid, transient increase in kidney ODC activity in intact mice; and 3) the ODC response to dehydration and the ODC response of intact mice to AVP are both blunted by propylthiouriucal treatment and acute gonadectomy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the effects of endogenous hormones and dehydration on renal ornithine de-carboxylase (EC 4.1.1.17) (ODC) in male mice.
the effects of dehydration and AVP on renal ODC.
the effects of endogenous hormonal status on the activity of the polyamine biosynthetic enzyme, ornithine decaboxylase (ODCase), in the kidney of male mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the renal ODC activity is regulated by a variety of endocrine factors.
AVP has a direct and rapid effect on renal ODC.
the renal ODC system is sensitive to the hormonal status of the animal and that the effects of dehydration are not mediated solely by AVP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kidney is a target organ for the action of AVP.

AVP is an acute regulator of renal ODC and that the effects of dehydration and other endocrinologically altered states on the enzyme are mediated by mechanisms that may involve the hypothalamus, the adrenal cortex, and the gonads.
the renal ornithine deacarboxylase activity is under control of the endocrine system, and the activity can be modulated by hormones such as vasopressin and glucocorticoids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kidney is a major site for the synthesis of polyamines in mice and that the hormonal status of the animal can influence the rate of synthesis.
the renal ODC response is a very sensitive indicator of hormonal status in the mouse kidney.
ODC activity in mouse kidneys is influenced by the hormonal status of the animal.
